questions.question: Interpret hierachial organization of life. / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Interpret hierarchical organization of life. /[CO1, CO2]
  • • It means that living organisms are structured in levels, starting from the smallest
  • (atoms → molecules → cells) and building up to larger, more complex levels
  • (tissues → organs → organisms → ecosystems ). Each level is made of the level
  • below it and works together to form the complete living system.

questions.question: Relate the purpose of global alignment in bioinformatics.
questions.solution_html:
• Relate the purpose of global alignment in bioinformatics /[CO6]
  • • It is used to compare two biological sequences end-to-end to see how similar they
  • are across their entire length. Its purpose is to identify overall similarity,
  • evolutionary relationships, and conserved regions between two full sequences.

questions.question: Define sequence identity.[5,6]
questions.solution_html:
• Sequence identity refers to the degree of similarity between the DNA or protein sequence
  • with another sequence or database sequences. It’s crucial for functional annotation,
  • structure prediction, establishing evolutionary relationships, disease diagnosis etc.
  • (5*2=10)

questions.question: How has the Human Genome Project impacted medicine? [5x2 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• How has the Human Genome Project impacted medicine? (K)/[C04]
  • • It transformed medicine by enabling personalized and predictive healthcare,
  • helped identify genes linked to diseases, improved diagnostic accuracy, guided
  • targeted drug development, and allowed early detection and prevention based on
  • a person’s genetic risk.
  • [5x210]
